pageTitle: A learning curve, built step by step.
pageIntro: A practical route from programming basics toward cloud and security, with small checkpoints along the way.
startingPoint: Early-stage Python learner, exploring computer science, Linux, networking, cloud, and security.
scheduleNote: These suggested check-in dates begin on 22 Nov 2026 and repeat about every four weeks. They are flexible markers, not deadlines; adjust them around schoolwork and exams.

stages.title: Python foundations
stages.summary: Get comfortable turning simple ideas into small programs.
stages.checkpoint: Write a few small Python programs and explain what each part does.

stages.title: Build a steady practice
stages.summary: Use repetition to make the programming basics feel familiar.
focus: Git basics and a simple README
stages.checkpoint: Save a handful of small exercises in a clearly organized repository.

stages.title: Linux and systems
stages.summary: Learn how to navigate a computer from the command line and see how its parts fit together.
stages.checkpoint: Complete a short set of repeatable command-line tasks and document them.

stages.title: Networking fundamentals
stages.summary: Understand the basic ideas behind how devices and websites communicate.
stages.checkpoint: Trace what happens when a browser opens a website and explain it simply.

stages.title: Security foundations
stages.summary: Build safe, practical security habits on top of systems and networking knowledge.
focus: Beginner exercises in safe learning labs
stages.checkpoint: Write a short security note explaining one concept and how to reduce its risk.

stages.title: Cloud fundamentals
stages.summary: Explore the building blocks that run applications and services in the cloud.
stages.checkpoint: Follow a beginner guide to deploy a small project and document each step.

stages.title: Build, reflect, and share
stages.summary: Bring one area of curiosity together in a project small enough to finish and explain.
focus: Build and write a clear README
stages.checkpoint: Publish one finished learning project with an honest account of what you learned.
